title: Infosys Started With ₹10,000. Its IPO Nearly Flopped
description:
Infosys started in 1981 with ₹10,000 that Sudha Murty gave her husband, Narayana Murthy, out of the ₹10,250 she had. He and six other engineers founded the company in Pune. In the year to March 2026 Infosys reported $20.2 billion in revenue (₹1.79 lakh crore). The road wasn't smooth: its 1993 public share sale only scraped through after Morgan Stanley bought 13% of the company. By 1999 it was the first India-registered company listed on Nasdaq.

The other side: Murthy later said keeping his wife, an engineer, out of the company was "wrongly idealistic" (CNBC-TV18, Jan 2024), and his 2023 call for young people to work 70 hours a week was criticised; an IT employees' union called a 70-hour week "illegal" (CNBC, Nov 2023). The lesson: you can start small, but expect years of work and near-misses.

Sources: Infosys Q4 FY2025-26 press release (23 Apr 2026); PTI via ThePrint (23 Apr 2026); Business Today (15 Mar 2024, Sudha Murty at the India Today Conclave; 4 Jan 2024, Murthy to CNBC-TV18; 9 Jan 2011, 1993 IPO); CNBC (6 Nov 2023); India Today (29 Mar 1999) on the Nasdaq listing; Infosys company history. 1 lakh crore = 1 trillion. Educational content, not investment advice.

scenes.say: Ten thousand rupees, nineteen eighty-one. Now twenty billion dollars a year. How?
That's Infosys, founded by Narayana Murthy and six other engineers.
The money came from his wife, Sudha Murty: almost everything she had.
But here's the catch: going public nearly flopped.
In nineteen ninety-three, it scraped through after Morgan Stanley bought thirteen percent.
